blocks.html: Bereshit/Genesis 24:55–67 — Rivkah’s family asks that she remain “ten days or so,” but the servant asks not to be delayed. When Rivkah is asked whether she will go with him, she answers, “I will go.” The servant then escorts her to Yitschaq, her bridegroom. This provides a possible prophetic pattern of the Bride remaining ready, answering the call and being gathered to Yeshua the Bridegroom on Yom Teruah, before the following ten-day period. The servant’s request not to be delayed also contrasts with the wicked servant’s thought, “My Master is delaying” (Mattithyahu/Matthew 24:48).

During this time, repentance remains urgent, faith is refined and allegiance is proven. Those who overcome remain faithful to Yeshua, keep יהוה’s commandments and receive the crown of life.

blocks.html: This exact future timetable remains interpretive, but the cumulative pattern is striking:
